job_title: Senior Lead, Global Semiconductor Category Manager
description: Company Description Sandisk understands how people and businesses consume data and we relentlessly innovate to deliver solutions that enable today’s needs and tomorrow’s next big ideas. With a rich history of groundbreaking innovations in Flash and advanced memory technologies, our solutions have become the beating heart of the digital world we’re living in and that we have the power to shape. Sandisk meets people and businesses at the intersection of their aspirations and the moment, enabling them to keep moving and pushing possibility forward. We do this through the balance of our powerhouse manufacturing capabilities and our industry-leading portfolio of products that are recognized globally for innovation, performance and quality. Sandisk has two facilities recognized by the World Economic Forum as part of the Global Lighthouse Network for advanced 4IR innovations. These facilities were also recognized as Sustainability Lighthouses for breakthroughs in efficient operations. With our global reach, we ensure the global supply chain has access to the Flash memory it needs to keep our world moving forward. Job Description Global Category Manager, PMIC & Mux The Senior Lead, Global Semiconductor Category Manager is responsible for defining and executing the global sourcing and supply strategy for assigned semiconductor commodities (e.g. PMIC & Mux). The GCM serves as the strategic owner of the category, ensuring long-term supply continuity, supplier competitiveness, technology alignment, and risk mitigation in support of Sandisk's customer commitments and business growth objectives. The role leads strategic supplier engagement, develops category roadmaps, drives sourcing decisions, and collaborates with Engineering, Operations, Finance, Planning, Supplier Quality, and Program teams to secure sustainable supply solutions. Essential Duties And Responsibilities Category Strategy & Business Planning Develop and maintain multi-year category strategies aligned with corporate objectives, product roadmaps, and customer demand forecasts. Analyze market conditions, supplier capabilities, capacity trends, technology roadmaps, geopolitical risks, and industry developments to guide sourcing decisions. Establish sourcing strategies that balance cost, supply assurance, technology leadership, and risk management. Lead category business reviews and provide executive updates regarding supply outlook, risks, and strategic initiatives Supply Continuity & Risk Management Own long-term supply continuity planning for assigned semiconductor categories. Drive supplier commitment strategies to support Sandisk's transition toward multi-year customer commitments. Lead risk identification, mitigation planning, allocation strategies, capacity reservation discussions, and business continuity planning. Escalate and drive resolution of strategic supply constraints with executive stakeholders and suppliers. Supplier Relationship Management Serve as the executive relationship owner for strategic semiconductor suppliers. Lead supplier negotiations covering commercial agreements, long-term capacity commitments, strategic investments, pricing frameworks, and supply assurance programs. Conduct Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and supplier performance assessments. Develop supplier roadmaps aligned with technology and business requirements. Strategic Sourcing & Qualification Lead sourcing recommendations for new programs and strategic component selections. Drive alternate source strategies, second-source qualifications, and supplier diversification initiatives. Partner with Engineering and NPI Procurement to influence sourcing decisions early in the product design cycle. Support value engineering initiatives focused on cost optimization, supply resilience, and technology competitiveness. Commercial Management Own strategic commercial negotiations for assigned semiconductor commodities. Lead cost reduction initiatives, supplier productivity programs, and long-term cost competitiveness strategies. Approve and manage PPV-related decisions and category-level cost performance reporting where applicable. Negotiate and support execution of NDAs, MSAs, SOWs, LTAs, LOAs, and other commercial agreements. Cross-Functional Leadership Partner closely with: Engineering and Platform Architecture NPI Procurement Planning and Material Management Supplier Quality Operations and Manufacturing Finance Program Management Provide strategic direction to Category Managers and Global Buyers responsible for tactical supplier execution. Key Deliverables Multi-year category strategy and roadmap Supply continuity plans supporting customer commitments Capacity and allocation management framework Strategic supplier relationship plans Second-source and qualification strategies Executive risk mitigation and escalation plans Commercial negotiation outcomes and savings initiatives Market intelligence and supplier technology Decision Authority The Global Category Manager Is Accountable For Category strategy and roadmap development Strategic sourcing recommendations Strategic supplier engagement and executive escalation Long-term supplier commitments and capacity planning Category-level risk management and mitigation Commercial negotiation strategy and major supplier agreements Cross-functional alignment on sourcing and supply Qualifications REQUIRED: Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or related discipline; MBA preferred. 10+ years of semiconductor sourcing, category management, supply chain, procurement, or supplier management experience. Strong understanding of semiconductor manufacturing ecosystems, especially PMIC & Mux. Experience managing executive-level supplier relationships and complex negotiations. Strong analytical, financial, and risk management capabilities. Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams and lead through ambiguity. Experience managing strategic supply continuity programs and high-impact business risks. We make energy work better for our customers, helping them thrive every day. That means always raising the bar - delivering better service and providing more reliable, resilient, and sustainable energy. Xcel Energy is a place where you’ll have opportunities to grow, expand your skills, and help lead the clean energy transition. We offer meaningful rewards, recognition, and support to help you build your career and make an impact - both on the job and beyond. Most importantly, it means you’ll be joining a company that knows employees are the driving force behind its success and is committed to helping you be your best. Senior Category Manager Position Summary Develop and execute sourcing category, supplier, and risk management strategies that align with business stakeholder priorities for key categories. Lead cross functional teams from the business and Supply Chain to drive successful project and category outcomes/results. Plan and lead competitive sourcing events using an enterprise-wide approach, incorporating external factors intelligence in support of category strategies. Develop effective negotiation strategies, plan, and conduct negotiations of commercial terms with suppliers to achieve category objectives. Lead on-going supplier performance, relationship, and development activities to ensure category strategy adherence. Develop and execute contracts with key suppliers. Direct Sourcing and Contracting support for third party contractor services including but not limited electric, gas and engineering functions. Essential Responsibilities Develop and implement enterprise-wide category strategies to optimize cost and improve operations in line with sourcing best practices. Collaborate with business stakeholders to align business demands, category/contract strategy, and execution. Perform spend and cost analysis (e.g. total cost of ownership and should cost models) and develop category strategies to achieve maximum value capture. Complete supplier research and risk profiles while monitoring industry information, external factors, and trends to ensure category strategies are aligned with current best practices. In conjunction with logistics personnel, implement optimal inventory strategies. Lead multiple strategic supplier performance, relationship and development management efforts focused on improving total cost of ownership, quality, delivery, and continuous improvement. Develop plans with suppliers that support business goals and strategies, while driving continuous improvement and collaboration to strengthen partnerships that bring value to the company and the supplier. Develop performance-based supplier scorecards. Monitor, document, and evaluate supplier performance. Lead the resolution of disputes with suppliers. Lead negotiations of commercial terms to establish contracts that support category strategies while meeting business requirements, including limits of liability and general terms & conditions. Review, analyze, verify, and negotiate contract changes or additional work orders. Monitor compliance across buying channel, supplier, and contract purchasing execution. Manage contractor claims to resolution and successfully minimize overall impact to cost and schedule. Ensure suppliers comply with contract terms and meet all commitments. Develop and communicate contract summary and implementation plans. Develop risk management strategies and in conjunction with Legal and Security teams, apply understanding of underlying principles of contract law to administer all category contract agreements. In collaboration with business area management, manage and define the risk elements of the contract Lead cross functional teams from the business and Supply Chain to drive successful project and category outcomes/results. Create and manage project plans to implement category strategies. Interacts with business leadership to integrate sourcing and business project plans. Manage Supply Chain, business, and supplier continuous improvement efforts. Lead change management efforts Minimum Requirements Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, business, or related technical/analytical field. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. Requires five years of supply chain experience with focus in sourcing. Three years of contract formation knowledge and experience. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and significant experience with purchasing and sourcing systems is required. Demonstrated customer service skills. Strong interpersonal and relationship skills are required. Required to attend meetings in various locations, up to 20% travel; driver's license required. Preferred Requirements MBA as well as Certified Professional in Supply Chain Management (CPSM) or other supply chain certification preferred. Negotiation and project management skills preferred. Previous experience managing categories with annual spend exceeding $100 million. description: LinkedIn is the world's largest professional network, built to create economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce. Our products help people make powerful connections, discover exciting opportunities, build necessary skills, and gain valuable insights every day. We're also committed to providing transformational opportunities for our own employees by investing in their growth. We aspire to create a culture that's built on trust, care, inclusion, and fun – where everyone can succeed. Join us to transform the way the world works. Job Description At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team. This role will be based in Mountain View, CA. We are looking for a Sr Commodity Manager / NPI lead to drive sourcing strategy, cost management, and supply assurance for our datacenter hardware portfolio. This role ensures we have secure, scalable, and cost-efficient access to critical components for new products that support LinkedIn's rapidly growing global compute footprint. In this role, you will collaborate closely with engineering, Capacity planning, finance, OxMs, and our global vendor ecosystem to deliver cost effective and reliable infrastructure at scale. Responsibilities: Commodity strategy and market intelligence - Develop and own the strategy across CPU, GPU, DRAM, NAND, HDD etc. Monitor market trends, silicon transitions, pricing cycles, supply health and technology roadmaps. Provide insights to inform LRP and annual hardware budget decisions. Supplier and Vendor Management for servers - Manage day-to-day and strategic relationships with suppliers across silicon, OxM and component vendors. Lead QBRs, roadmap alignment sessions and performance scorecards. Drive escalations to resolve supply, quality or commercials. Supply Assurance and Allocations - Secure quarterly and annual supply allocations with commodity and OxM vendors, partner with supply planning to ensure accuracy in consumption and forecast to prevent shortages. Mitigate risk for long lead time items, partnering with engineering on SKU selection. Cost and Commercial Ownership - Lead negotiations including pricing, LTAs, volume discounts, rebates. Develop cost models to influence engineering decisions and identify cost optimizations through multi vendor strategies and roadmap optimization. Quality reliability and lifecycle management - Oversee product qualification in partnership with Hardware engineering to influence architecture decisions and vendor selection. Drive quality improvements, RMA terms, AFR metrics and supplier corrective actions. Drive decisions on EOL transitions, component refresh cycle, and adoption of new technology. Cross functional leadership - Work closely with engineering to influence hardware architecture decisions and vendor selection. Partner with capacity planning, supply planning and DC operations to understand deployment needs / timelines. Collaborate with finance on cost forecast and CapEx modeling. Qualifications Basic Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field 12+ years of experience in commodity management, vendor management and hardware sourcing or supply chain for datacenter/enterprise. Experience managing silicon, memory and storage components Background in silicon lifecycles, DRAM/NAND market dynamics and datacenter hardware architecture. Background in negotiations and ability to manage executive level relationships. Experience leading complex technical programs in compute, storage, or networking hardware Demonstrated analytical skills with ability to model cost, supply and risk tradeoffs. Experience working with suppliers, contract manufacturers, and global production teams Preferred Qualifications: Master’s degree in an engineering discipline Experience with hyperscale infrastructure or data center environments Demonstrated ability to work closely with C-level executives, particularly in the OxM and Commodity supplier space, to ensure alignment on NPI roadmaps and best in class pricing/availability Experience with ERP solutions and hardware PLM tools Demonstrated ability to influence decision-making across engineering, operations, and sourcing Experience with infrastructure supply ecosystem and risk mitigation strategies Suggested Skills: Systems Thinking Cross-functional Communication Stakeholder Management Hardware Infrastructure You will Benefit from our Culture: We strongly believe in the well-being of our employees and their families. We engineer and build advanced, sound-attenuated, temperature-controlled generator sets designed to perform in the toughest environments. Backed by industry-leading service and real-time telemetry technology, we give our customers the confidence and visibility they need to keep critical operations running. At Mesa, People Come First. Values Drive Everything We Do. We Are: Action-Oriented. Disciplined. Accountable. Passionate. Trustworthy. What We Offer Competitive base pay 401(k) plan Generous paid time off — including vacation, holidays, parental leave, and bereavement 100% employer-paid Health, Dental, and Vision insurance for employees and their dependents Employee Assistance Program Life Insurance Short- and Long-Term Disability coverage Critical Illness and Accident insurance Annual Evaluations with the opportunity for a pay increase based on performance We invest in our people because they are the foundation of our success. Positions identified as safety-sensitive require initial drug screening as a condition of employment, and employees in those roles may be subject to random testing in accordance with company policy. If you’re ready to do meaningful work, grow professionally, and be part of a team that’s powering critical industries nationwide, this is your opportunity. Join Mesa Power Solutions and help us build the future of reliable power. Job Summary The Senior Category Manager provides strategic leadership and direction for category management and strategic sourcing across Mesa Power Solutions' multi-site manufacturing operations. This role owns the development and execution of comprehensive category strategies spanning mechanical, electrical, fuel-system, engine, and ancillary components used in gas engine power generation equipment - with an expanded scope that includes capital equipment, engineered systems, and strategic supplier partnerships critical to Mesa's growth trajectory. Building on the Category Manager role, the Senior Category Manager leads enterprise-wide sourcing transformations, mentors other category managers, and serves as a key procurement liaison to executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. This position drives total cost of ownership optimization, supply chain resilience, supplier innovation, and strategic risk management aligned to corporate growth objectives and new product introduction (NPI) roadmaps. Essential Duties Develop and execute multi-year category strategies across mechanical, electrical, engine, fuel system, rotating equipment, and related components, with a total cost of ownership focus. Lead enterprise-wide strategic sourcing initiatives, including spend analysis, category assessments, sourcing roadmaps, and supplier selection. Own the full category management lifecycle, including market intelligence, demand planning, RFx processes, negotiations, contracting, and implementation. Establish category governance frameworks, performance metrics, and executive reporting to drive accountability and results. Manage executive-level supplier relationships, including business reviews, scorecards, strategic development plans, and performance improvement initiatives. Drive supplier consolidation, capability development, technology advancement, and capacity expansion while ensuring supply continuity and quality. Lead complex commercial negotiations and manage master supply agreements, long-term contracts, pricing structures, SLAs, KPIs, risk allocation, and compliance requirements. Conduct should-cost analyses, total cost modeling, and value-based negotiations to achieve savings and improve commercial outcomes. Develop and execute supplier risk management and supply chain resilience strategies, including dual sourcing, contingency planning, and disruption recovery efforts. Monitor market, commodity, regulatory, and geopolitical trends impacting supply continuity and provide risk mitigation recommendations to leadership. Partner with engineering, operations, quality, logistics, finance, and legal teams to support new product introduction, capital projects, component standardization, and value engineering initiatives. Lead cost reduction, lead time improvement, and operational efficiency programs that deliver measurable business value. Mentor category managers and procurement team members, establish sourcing best practices, drive tool and process adoption, manage savings to targets, and ensure compliance with procurement policies and regulatory requirements. All other duties assigned. Qualifications Education Required 4 Year / Bachelors Degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field from an accredited university. Preferred Graduate Degree or relevant advanced degree (e.g., MS in Supply Chain Management, Engineering Management). Experience Required 8 years of procurement/category management experience in industrial manufacturing, heavy equipment, or power generation 8 years of demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional sourcing projects with measurable cost savings and supplier performance improvements. 8 years of experience negotiating master supply agreements and long-term contracts with strategic suppliers. Preferred 10 years of procurement/category management experience in industrial manufacturing, heavy equipment, or power generation. 5 years of experience with gas engines, rotating equipment, or reciprocating engine systems. 5 years of prior experience mentoring or leading a team of category managers or sourcing professionals. 8 years of experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations across multiple U.S. locations. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. The successful candidate will rely on their combination of business acumen, technical depth, innate curiosity, and experience across raw materials categories to bring strategic approaches and oversight to the sourcing of these critical components, while developing and maintaining positive, productive relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners alike. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with a breakthrough technology and an incredible mission! Relocation assistance is available. description: About Lucid At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. The team partners closely with Engineering, Supplier Industrialization, Finance, Logistics, Quality, Legal, and Manufacturing to translate product requirements into executable sourcing and production plans. Its work spans strategy through launch and mass production, combining deep supplier engagement, manufacturing knowledge, commercial judgment, and data-driven analysis to protect continuity, cost, quality, and timing. About The Role Lucid is seeking a seasoned Senior Global Supply Manager to lead the High Voltage Electromechanical commodity portfolio within the High Voltage Powertrain Systems team. description: Description AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. Amazon Web Services (AWS) provides a highly reliable, scalable, and low-cost cloud platform that powers thousands of businesses in over 190 countries. AWS Infrastructure Service (AIS) organization works to deliver cutting-edge solutions to source, build and maintain our socially responsible data center supply chains. We are a team of highly-motivated, engaged, and responsive professionals who enable the core sustainable infrastructure of AWS. Come join our team and be a part of history as we deliver results for the largest cloud services company on Earth! The AIS Power & Cooling team is looking for a results-oriented individual to own sourcing and supply management for Data Center Power & Cooling Equipment. Our Category Managers are experts in their industries who deliver the supply that helps drive the explosive growth of AWS. As a member of the Power and Cooling Procurement Team, you will manage the end-to-end global sourcing and supply chain for one or more of the categories that reside within the Power and Cooling Equipment space supporting AWS Data Center build projects. description: The Company Saildrone is a maritime defense company and the global leader in autonomous unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). With more ocean miles and real-world operational experience than any USV manufacturer or operator, Saildrone maintains active, combat-deployed systems supporting national security and force projection around the world, 24/7/365. Saildrone’s manufacturing and R&D headquarters are located in Alameda, CA, with business development and sales operations in Washington, DC, and deployment hubs in Europe and the Middle East. By combining proven autonomous operations, edge computing, advanced sensing, renewable power, and the most advanced and robust unmanned surface technology on the planet, Saildrone is shaping how the Navy of the future operates. Join a fast-moving, mission-driven team at the forefront of maritime security and autonomous innovation. THE POSITION We are seeking a highly motivated and strategic Senior Global Supply Manager (Sr GSM) to join our supply chain team. As a Sr GSM, you will own the end-to-end sourcing and supply chain strategy for critical commodities. You will be the bridge between our Engineering, NPI (New Product Introduction), and Production teams, ensuring that we deliver high-quality products on time and at the right cost. The ideal candidate has a proven track record in hardware manufacturing, a deep understanding of supplier capabilities, and the hustle required to build supply chain processes from the ground up in a startup setting. THE TEAM The Supply Chain Team procures the essential materials required to build our drone fleet. Operating within the high-stakes national security and defense sector, we are dedicated to scaling our supply base and optimizing operations to meet the growing demands of the business. The Responsibilities Strategic Sourcing: Identify, evaluate, and onboard suppliers that align with our engineering requirements, quality standards, and scaling roadmaps. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Hardware Engineering and Production teams during the NPI phase to drive design-for-manufacturability (DFM) and ensure supply chain readiness. Negotiation & Contracting: Lead complex negotiations for pricing, lead times, and terms. Partner with Legal to establish NDAs, Master Supply Agreements (MSAs), and Statements of Work (SOWs). Cost Management: Develop and execute cost-reduction strategies. Perform "should-cost" modeling, Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis, and manage RFQs to optimize our Bill of Materials (BOM) costs. Risk Mitigation: Monitor the global commodity landscape for potential disruptions. Proactively develop secondary sources and risk-mitigation plans to ensure uninterrupted production. Supplier Relationship Management: Build and maintain strong partnerships with supplier executive teams. Drive supplier performance through regular business reviews (QBRs) focusing on quality, delivery, and cost metrics. Leadership & Process Scaling: Mentor mid/junior Global Supply Managers, establish standardized sourcing playbooks, and scale procurement systems as the department expands. Lead supplier negotiations covering pricing, commercial terms, Long-Term Agreements (LTAs), payment terms, and other key commercial requirements. Collaborate globally with FE Materials Operations, Technology Development/Material Procurement, engineering, quality, manufacturing and other procurement partners. Provide fact-based recommendations and market intelligence to senior leadership on strategic category and supplier decisions. description: About ITT ITT Inc. (NYSE: ITT) is a diversified global leading manufacturer of highly engineered critical components and customized technology solutions serving the flow, aerospace and defense, transportation, industrial, and energy markets. Through operational execution, innovation, and disciplined capital deployment, including strategic acquisitions such as SPX FLOW, ITT partners with its customers to deliver enduring solutions to the key industries that underpin our modern way of life. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, ITT has a market cap of roughly $20 billion and employs more than 15,000 people across 40 countries and serves customers in approximately 125 countries. Following the acquisition of SPX FLOW, the company is expected to generate $5.4 billion in annual revenue. Our businesses are organized in three distinct segments, each based around our core engineering DNA: Flow Technologies: A global leader in, providing a broad portfolio of pumps, valves, mixing and agitation equipment, heat transfer, homogenizers, separation, water and wastewater treatment, and engineered process solutions.Our leading brands include the iconic Goulds Pumps (with more than 175 years of history), Anhydro, APV, Bornemann, Bran+Luebbe, C’treat, Engineered Valves, Gerstenberg Schröder, Habonim, Johnson Pump, Lightnin, Philadelphia, Plenty, PRO Cast, Rheinhütte, Seital Separation, Stelzer, Svanehøj, Tigerholm, Uutechnic, VIDAR, Waukesha Cherry-Burrell. Motion Technologies: A global leader in brake pads (ICE and electrified brake pads) and shock absorbers (energy absorption solutions) for transportation applications. Our leading brands include Friction Technologies, KONI and Axtone. Connect and Control Technologies: A leader in critical applications for the aerospace, defense and industrial markets, including harsh environment connectors and control components. Our leading brands include ITT Cannon, Enidine, Aerospace Controls and kSARIA. Position Summary Reporting directly to the Director, S trategic Sourcing for ITT (Connect & Control Technologies), the Global Sourcing Manager is a critical member of the Global Supply Management group responsible for enhancing overall supply chain performance through the effective management of ~$ 3 00M in global spend. This role is responsible for implementing ITT’s business strategy to your assigned categories and maintaining the best sources of supply. The Global Sourcing Manager is responsible for building strong supplier relationships and being proactive in mitigating supply chain challenges due to emerging economic trends around pricing, logistics , and geo-political risks. Working collaboratively with cross functional teams, this role will identify and champion complexity - reduction initiatives that will enhance profitability and service to customers. This is an on-site position that can be located in Orchard Park, Valencia, Irvine, or El Cajon, CA with up to 50% travel. Essential Responsibilities For the assigned categories, develop and implement sourcing / supply chain strategies to harness economies of scale, drive economic value, manage supply chain risk, and enable business growth at a global level in a multi-market-culture environment. Lead complex and critical negotiations utilizing extensive professional knowledge of principles and techniques of negotiation in the purchasing cycle. Provide global leadership for the major OEM suppliers. Research and evaluate suppliers based on price, quality, selection, service, support, availability, reliability, production and distribution capabilities, and the supplier's reputation and history. Leverage supplier management, category / commodity management and total cost principles to oversee the supplier selection process within the respective businesses / sites and encourage productive relationships with appropriate suppliers that drive meaningful value. Search, identify , qualify, develop, and manage suppliers to secure the best possible terms (cost, payment, inventory, etc . ) while ensuring operational performance (quality, OTD, lead time, cost, etc . ). Partner with engineering, manufacturing, quality and other category managers to drive value analysis and engineering (VAVE) savings. Partner with NPD teams to obtain early supplier engagement to set expectations, optimize quality, supply reliability, while reducing risk and cost for new product launches. Identify and introduce new materials, technologies, and supply chain capabilities to meet current and future needs of ITT products. Other responsibilities as assigned . Position Requirements Bachelor’s degree from an accredited 4-year college or university in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or equivalent is required . Minimum of 10 years of broad and global sourcing leadership experience, preferably in a highly regulated manufacturing organization, across a large multi-location, global business. Global Sourcing contract negotiation skills. Experience in a mixed mode manufacturing environment, Engineer to Order, Low Volume / High Mix, and Configure to Order environment. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to effectively interact with all levels of external and internal customers and stakeholders. Demonstrated experience influencing executives. Working knowledge of Lean practices such as Daily Management, Standard Work, Kaizen, Heijunka , Poka- yoke, and Gemba. Experience with a variety of commodities , including, but not limited to: precision metal machining, composites and plastics, injection molding, electronics and cables . Drive performance with a sense of urgency and a commitment to work together as a team to achieve results. D emonstrated success in a large-scale, global organization with the ability to work at both the strategic and detailed level. English fluency is required , while ability to communicate in one or more of the following languages is highly beneficial: German, Italian, French, Chinese (Mandarin / Cantonese) Travel up to 50% This position requires use of information which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. persons within the meaning of ITAR . ITAR defines a U.S. person as a U.S. Citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident ( i.e. 'Green Card Holder'), Political Asylee, or Refugee. Safety is a core value at ITT. Our employees understand and follow all ITT safety policies and procedures, participate in workplace inspections, safety training, and in the development of job safety analyses. Equal Pay Act Statement We aim to pay our ‘ITT’ers’ fairly and competitively in the locations that they live and work. Pay-for-performance is a principle that we believe in, and employees are rewarded based not only on ‘what’ they accomplish, but also on ‘how’ they reflect ITT’s values. ITT offers a competitive salary and robust total rewards package, such as health insurance, 401(k), short and long-term disability, paid time off, growth and developmental opportunities, and other incentive compensation programs. Specific benefits are dependent upon whether or not the position is part of a collective-bargaining agreement. The salary offered to a candidate is based several factors such as candidate experience and qualifications, location, as well as market and business considerations. Equal Pay Act Range Annual Salary Range is from $119,400.00 to $178,200.00, plus benefits & incentive plan.

description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About The Team Procurement is part of Stripe Finance and owns the full supplier lifecycle and buying journey. The team sources and evaluates new vendors, renews and negotiates contracts with existing suppliers, and leads third‑party risk management and compliance activities to ensure suppliers meet Stripe’s standards. Procurement also drafts, reviews, and approves supplier contract structures and terms, aligned with Stripe’s risk appetite and legal requirements. What you’ll do We are looking for an experienced Sourcing professional to focus on establishing trusted business partner relationships in the technology space at Stripe with a “users first” approach to ensure early and active participation across the full lifecycle of strategic sourcing and procurement, including: category planning, sourcing strategies, RFx execution, supplier evaluation and selection, contract negotiations and management, and continuous improvements. You will play a critical role in ensuring Stripe's procurement aligns with our operational principles by contributing to our sustainable growth while fostering strong, ethical supplier relationships. Experience with complex software negotiations is required. Responsibilities Develop and execute strategic sourcing plans for designated categories, identifying opportunities for cost reduction, quality improvement, and process efficiencies Lead supplier selection, assessment, and contract negotiation processes, ensuring compliance with Stripe's policies and risk management protocols Conduct market research and analysis to inform category strategies and stay ahead of industry trends Be an active champion across the company supporting our third party risk programs and fiscal initiatives when engaging in Procurement activities Deliver on strategic sourcing management goals including cost savings and spend under management, and implement any necessary process enhancements to ensure that those goals are achieved Evaluate existing supplier base and identify rationalization and/or RFx opportunities in partnership with business teams and Finance, allowing Stripe to maximize negotiating leverage Work closely with internal teams to drive enterprise-level procurement solutions and increase supplier management effectiveness Participate in establishing short-term and long range planning and budget development of the company to support strategic business goals Help to develop and execute a roadmap to build and scale an impactful Strategic Sourcing & Category Management function that Stripes recognize and value Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum Requirements A minimum of 8 years of experience in indirect sourcing, procurement, category management, or a related field Demonstrated ability to develop and implement strategic sourcing and category management strategies Proven negotiation skills and a track record of achieving significant cost savings and supplier value without compromising on quality or service Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage and interpret complex data Experience in supplier contracting with a solid understanding of standard commercial terms and conditions to mitigate risks and create clear service level agreements Leadership and stakeholder management skills with the ability to elevate ambitions and influence cross-functional and internal team members Preferred Qualifications Solution-oriented mindset with enthusiasm for establishing best practice Self-disciplined, diligent, proactive and detail oriented Comfort with a rapid pace of change, complexity, and working across matrixed functions, preferably within a fast-paced technology or financial services environment Strategic mindset with the ability to make sound business decisions based on data and analytics Understanding or experience with e-procurement tools and systems (e.g., Zip, Workday Strategic Sourcing, Oracle, etc.) Familiarity with the fintech industry and its supply chain and procurement challenges In-office expectations Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible. Pay and benefits The annual US base salary range for this role is $136,000 - $204,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process. Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends. We look forward to hearing from you. At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us. Apply now Please find our California applicant personal information notice here.

description: Shape the Future with Us. At Lubrizol, we’re bringing to life the chemistry behind clean water, efficient transportation, reliable infrastructure, critical medicines, and the products people rely on every day through science, sustainability, and a culture of inclusion. As part of our global team, you’ll be empowered to make a real impact - on your career, your community, and the world around you. Job Type: Full-time. Collaborate in person 4 days each week, with 1 flexible remote day. Location: Deer Park, TX How You'll Make An Impact As a Procurement Manager – Facilities & MRO, you'll be at the center of driving operational excellence across our manufacturing and corporate sites. You'll shape sourcing strategies, build high-value supplier partnerships, and lead initiatives that improve reliability, efficiency, and sustainability across critical Facilities and Maintenance, Repair & Operations (MRO) categories. In this highly visible role, you'll partner with leaders across the organization to solve complex business challenges, optimize supplier networks, support major site investments, and deliver measurable value through strategic procurement. From ensuring critical services are available when needed to helping manufacturing operations reduce risk and improve performance, your contributions will have a direct and lasting impact on business success, employee experience, and customer satisfaction. In This Role, You Will Lead regional and global category strategies for Facilities Services, Maintenance, Repair and Operations (MRO), Site Services, and Capital Project support. Develop and execute category plans aligned with business objectives, operational priorities, cost management goals, and procurement strategies. Conduct complex commercial negotiations for facilities management services, maintenance contracts, technical service agreements, and MRO supply partnerships. Identify and deliver value through total cost of ownership initiatives, supplier consolidation, demand planning, inventory optimization, and process improvements. Partner with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Environmental, Health, Safety and Sustainability (EHSS), Finance, and Legal teams to meet site and business requirements. Monitor and report key performance indicators related to cost savings, supplier performance, service quality, compliance, inventory management, and risk mitigation. Assess and mitigate supplier, operational, safety, contractual, financial, and supply continuity risks through proactive category management. Build strategic supplier relationships and lead governance and performance review processes that drive accountability and continuous improvement. Manage sourcing events including Requests for Information (RFIs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and Requests for Proposals (RFPs). Support business continuity through supplier qualification, contingency planning, and robust risk management practices. Champion sustainability, operational reliability, and stakeholder satisfaction through continuous improvement initiatives. Required Qualifications That Enable Your Success Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience. Five or more years of experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, supply chain, category management, manufacturing, facilities management, or operations. Experience managing Facilities, MRO, Industrial Services, Engineering, Operations, or other indirect spend categories. Demonstrated success leading supplier negotiations, contract management activities, and supplier performance programs. Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills. Experience leading cross-functional projects and influencing decision-makers across multiple levels of an organization. Ability to collaborate effectively across regions, cultures, and functional teams within a matrixed environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and digital procurement systems. Preferred Qualifications That Drive You Forward Master of Business Administration (MBA) or other advanced degree. Experience supporting manufacturing sites, engineering organizations, industrial operations, or plant environments. Knowledge of MRO supply chains, reliability and maintenance practices, inventory management, or facilities management. Experience negotiating facilities management, industrial services, maintenance, or technical service contracts Experience using SAP or other enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems. Professional certifications such as Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM), Certified Purchasing Manager (CPM), Certified Professional Maintenance Manager (CPMM), International Facility Management Association (IFMA), Certified Facility Manager (CFM), or equivalent. Advanced training in sourcing, supplier relationship management, or commercial negotiations. Spanish bilingual verbal and written communication skills. Your Work Environment Role At Lubrizol, we’re committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and empowering environment where you can do your best work—whether in a lab, on the production floor, or in a hybrid office setting. Depending on your role, your work environment may include: Standing, walking, or operating equipment for extended periods Working in a lab or manufacturing setting with appropriate PPE provided Use of computers and digital tools in an office or hybrid environment Occasional lifting or movement of materials Adherence to rigorous safety protocols and ergonomic standards We continuously invest in our facilities and technologies to ensure they support your well-being, productivity, and growth. If you require reasonable accommodation, we are committed to working with you to ensure an inclusive and accessible experience. Benefits That Empower You Competitive salary with performance-based bonus plans 401(k) match + Age-Weighted Defined Contribution Comprehensive medical, dental & vision coverage Health Savings Account (HSA) Paid holidays, vacation, and parental leave Flexible work environment Learning and development opportunities Career and professional growth Inclusive culture and vibrant community engagement Learn more at https://benefits.lubrizol.com/! Lubrizol: Imagined for Life. Enabled by Science. ™ Delivered by You. For nearly 100 years, The Lubrizol Corporation, a Berkshire Hathaway company, has been at the forefront of innovation to enhance everyday life, advance mobility, and make the modern world work better. Our specialty chemistry solutions—from engine oils, performance coatings, and skincare to medical devices and plumbing systems —are powered by the expertise, passion, and commitment of people like you. We tackle the world’s toughest challenges with science-based solutions, deeply understanding our customers to deliver innovative chemistry and differentiated value. Our inclusive culture, dedication to safety, and incredible global talent drive our success. Our solutions meet the evolving needs of the modern world—brought to life by science and, most importantly, delivered by you. Whether you're in the lab, on the production floor, or in the office, you'll be part of a team around the world that empowers you to think boldly, drive results, and contribute to solutions that shape a better, more sustainable future. We win because of you. Let’s build the future together.

description: Job Description About Sally Beauty Holdings, Inc. At SBH, our purpose is to inspire a more colorful, confident, and welcoming world. We are the leader in professional hair color, selling and distributing professional beauty supplies across 11 countries through our Sally Beauty and Beauty Systems Group businesses. Sally Beauty offers products for hair color, hair care, nails, and skin care to retail customers looking for salon-quality products at a value price. Beauty Systems Group, branded as Cosmo Prof or Armstrong McCall stores, along with its direct sales consultants, sell professionally branded products intended for use and resale by salons to retail consumers. This is a hybrid role reporting into our office at Legacy West in Plano Texas. Essential Functions Responsible for the development and implementation of an overall procurement/sourcing strategy in a multi -sourced environment. Evaluates and determines the most cost-effective and efficient means of sourcing, acquiring and delivering products and services, including international procurement for private label brands. Manages and controls the contractual relationship with service providers and vendors that reflect their specific area. Responsible for the development and implementation of category management processes based on industry best standards. Works with leadership and is responsible for the development and execution of the procurement strategy which aligns and supports the business strategies. Provides financial reporting and fiscal savings for the procurement organization, onboarding suppliers and SBH directed projects. The Procurement Manager will keep pace with the demands of a dynamic business climate, anticipate problems and develop appropriate solutions, and provide the leadership necessary to effectively implement these initiatives. Primary Duties 25% Implements departmental Policies and Procedures which align with SBH corporate goals, and allow for effective procurement of all required Private Label good for sale, in accordance with industry best practices. This will include assisting in the procurement of Private Label product for international segments. 25% Develops, plans, organizes and implements procurement strategies and programs to increase operational efficiency, as well as to mitigate risk to SBH members and other stakeholders. Able to analyze inventory, forecasting, demand and program schedules in order to manage capacity and material availability with the supply base. Understands capacity requirements and supply base capacity. 10% Manages all activities of responsible area of the procurement department, including the identifying cost drivers, executing Request for Information (RFIs), Request for Proposal (RFPs) and business cases. 10% Leads procurement analysis, supplier development and implementation of SOW (statement of Work) for procurement. Provide develops / audits procurement orders for accuracy and compliance. 10% Material / Component Lifecycle Management. Defines and manages appropriate supplier QBRs. Creates, negotiates and incorporates contract amendments, renegotiating contracts, if required, to accommodate scope changes or changes in organization requirement. Minimum of 5 - 7 years of business experience responsible for supplier onboarding, procurement, spend metrics and management experience. Minimum of 3 - 5 years of managing staff and interacting with management. An in-depth understanding of industry standards as they apply to the Procurement and Supply Chain. Experience developing and using Key Performance Indicators to manage the procurement process. Experience with sourcing business systems, equipment and services for the business. Compentencies/Attributes Must have a basic understanding of all procurement product, services, and knowledge of technology. Demonstrates practical knowledge of procurement/sourcing best practices. Understands and anticipates customer and consumer needs. Takes action to meet customer and consumer expectations, needs, and concerns. Demonstrates persuasion and influencing skills with adeptness in conflict management. Has leadership skills to help train and groom staff for their development. In addition, associates of SBH may take advantage of our in house salon with complementary services and a varied selection of food options at our corporate campus. Also, featured at our corporate campus, is both a Sally Beauty and CosmoProf Professional onsite store, where associates enjoy a great merchandise discount!

description: Activités S UMMARY : To purchase requisitioned material and execute strategic sourcing initiatives to support scheduled assembly and spares requirements to meet customer needs while proactively mitigating geopolitical, macroeconomic, and supply chain disruptions. Reschedule and update purchase orders due to changes dictated by engineering change orders. description: Job Title: Integrated Business Planning Analyst Location: Remote Department: Integrated Business Planning Reports To: Sr. Manager, Demand Planning Job Summary The Integrated Business Planning (IBP) Analyst plays a critical role in balancing supply and demand across regions, channels, and product lines. description: SIOP Forecast Analyst - Safety & Racing Job Description Holley Performance Brands, founded in 1903, is a leading designer, manufacturer, and marketer of high-performance automotive aftermarket products. Our portfolio of iconic brands powers enthusiasts and racers worldwide—from classic muscle and modern performance to off-road and powersports—combining a rich heritage of innovation with a passion for performance. This role sits in the Safety & Racing division, located in New Braunfels, TX—home to Simpson, HRX, Stilo, HANS, and RaceQuip—where a single SIOP process aligns demand and supply planning across all five brands. Position Summary: The SIOP Analyst is the analytical engine of the Safety & Racing division's Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP) process. The division owns and runs SIOP for its brands, and this role gives division leadership the forecasts, dashboards, and single demand plan they need to stay in control of demand and supply decisions across Simpson, HRX, Stilo, HANS, and RaceQuip. Reporting to the division's Sales & Operations Coordinator—with a dotted line to the Corporate SIOP Leader for standards and alignment—the analyst turns operational data into decision-ready insight. They build the forecasts, run the numbers behind the monthly demand review, surface inventory and capacity risks early, and translate complex analysis into a clear business narrative that improves forecast accuracy, inventory performance, production planning, and customer service. This role is not eligible for remote work. This position will be based in our New Braunfels, TX office . Key Responsibilities: Run the Division's SIOP Process Coordinate the monthly SIOP cycle for the division, consolidating Sales, Marketing, Finance, Operations, Production, Purchasing, and Customer Service inputs into one division demand plan. Prepare the analysis, dashboards, and materials behind the monthly demand and consensus reviews, and present risks, opportunities, and recommendations to division leadership. Keep the process aligned to corporate SIOP standards and cadence while ensuring the plan reflects division priorities. Drive accountability to the agreed plan across brands and functions. Forecasting & Demand Analysis Produce and maintain the demand forecasts across all five brands, selecting and segmenting statistical models to fit each brand's demand behavior. Forecast new product introductions and phase-in / phase-out transitions with Marketing and Product. Track forecast accuracy and bias, analyze variances, and recommend corrective actions. Factor order trends, seasonality, and motorsports event schedules into the plan. Data, Dashboards & Tools Build and maintain the data models and business logic behind the forecast, turning raw sales, shipment, and point-of-sale history into forecast-ready datasets. Develop the dashboards and reporting that make division SIOP performance visible (Excel, Power BI, Tableau, SQL, DAX, Power Query). Automate recurring data preparation, model refresh, and exception reporting. Partner with IT to keep data clean, governed, and integrated with the ERP. Inventory & Supply Alignment Analyze inventory to flag excess, shortages, slow-moving, and obsolete stock, and translate the demand plan into inventory targets. Maintain planning parameters—safety stock, days of supply, reorder points—balancing service level against working capital. Work with Purchasing to surface material shortages that threaten deliveries, and recommend expedite, defer, and cancel actions. Continuous Improvement & Systems Maintain data integrity across ERP, forecasting, and reporting systems. Help set and maintain the division's forecasting standards and playbooks, and support upcoming ERP upgrades. Benchmark and report forecast performance to keep it visible across the division. What You Bring: Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business/Data Analytics, Operations Management, Engineering, Finance, mathematics, statistics, or a related field. 2–5 years in supply chain analytics, SIOP, demand planning, forecasting, inventory management, or business analytics. Experience supporting a consensus, SIOP, or S&OP demand process. Working knowledge of statistical forecasting methods and planning parameters (safety stock, days of supply, reorder points). Advanced Excel (PivotTables, Power Query, XLOOKUP, formulas), plus forecasting software and PowerPoint. Experience with an ERP system (Infor SyteLine/LN or comparable) and BI reporting (Power BI, Tableau, or similar). Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to align stakeholders across functions and brands. Comfort managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Bonus Points For: APICS/ASCM (CPIM, CSCP) or IBF (CPF/ACPF) certification. Experience supporting SIOP or Integrated Business Planning (IBP). Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous-improvement experience in planning. Experience across multiple sites, brands, or business units. Experience supporting an ERP implementation or upgrade. Advanced analytics (SQL, DAX, Power Query, Python, or R) applied to forecasting. Background in automotive aftermarket, powersports, racing/motorsports safety, or high-SKU consumer products. Technical Skills: Microsoft Excel (Advanced) Microsoft Power BI Power Query SQL / DAX (preferred) ERP systems Microsoft PowerPoint Microsoft Teams Forecasting and demand planning software Data visualization and dashboard development Key Performance Indicators: Forecast Accuracy and Bias Inventory Turns Inventory Days on Hand (DOH) On-Time Delivery Customer Fill Rate Production Schedule Adherence Inventory Accuracy Backorder Reduction Configured Order Lead Time Data Accuracy and Reporting Timeliness Why Holley Is a Great Place to Work At Holley, we’re more than a performance parts company—we’re a community of enthusiasts, innovators, and problem-solvers. We offer a competitive benefits package and a culture that values both performance and people. Benefits: Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one. 401(k) with company match Paid time off and 9 paid holidays Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Company-paid life and short-term disability insurance Employee discounts on Holley Performance Brands products, events, and partnerships Education Assistance program Holley is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. If you require assistance or accommodation due to a disability during the application process, please contact human resources.

description: Role Summary The Demand Planning Analyst provides analytical and operational support to the Demand Planning team by developing baseline forecasts, analyzing demand trends, maintaining planning data, and preparing reports and insights that support the monthly demand consensus process. Support new product launches, product transitions, and product discontinuations from a demand planning perspective. Develop and automate reporting using Excel, Power BI, and other emerging AI-enabled analytical tools. Experience using Power BI. Experience in a manufacturing environment. Knowledge of forecasting methodologies and SIOP processes. Success Measures Improved forecast accuracy and reduced forecast bias. Timely completion of monthly forecasting activities. High-quality analytical support for Senior Demand Planners. Increased automation and reporting efficiency. Accurate and reliable planning data. Identification of demand risks and opportunities before they impact the business.

description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About You And The Role We’re hiring a Global Supply Manager to own end-to-end commodity strategy and supplier performance for mission-critical hardware that enables Zipline’s autonomous aircraft and global delivery operations. You will operate at the intersection of manufacturing ramp execution, product engineering, and global sourcing—delivering reliable, scalable supply for systems where component failure or late deliveries directly impact flight operations and customer outcomes. This is an in-person role based at our HQ in South San Francisco with regular on-site supplier engagements and 20–30% travel to supplier sites across North America, Asia, and Europe. What You'll Do Own one or more critical commodity/category portfolios (examples: avionics/electronics assemblies, motors/actuators, battery packs, composite airframe structures, or machined flight-critical components) end-to-end: sourcing strategy, supplier selection, contract terms, qualification, ramp to volume, and long-term supplier development. Set and deliver measurable targets within your portfolio: first-year goals for cost reduction (%), supplier on-time delivery (OTD) improvement points, quality reduction targets (PPM), qualification cycle-time, and ramp throughput milestones. Own missed-target escalation and recovery plans. Lead competitive source selection and negotiations for multi-year, multi-million-dollar supply agreements, including pricing, capacity commitments, lead-time guarantees, penalties, and IP/technical data rights where applicable. Manage supplier qualification and performance: drive PPAP/qualification plans, scorecards, QBRs, corrective action plans, and on-site audits to hold suppliers to AS9100/ISO9001 quality and traceability expectations when required. Integrate with Engineering, Supplier Industrialization, Manufacturing Operations, Materials Planning, and Program Management to translate design and production requirements into supplier deliverables, readiness gates, and acceptance criteria; be the primary commercial and operational owner during design-to-production transitions. Architect and execute risk mitigation strategies (dual sourcing, inventory buffers, localization, vertical integration assessments) and manage supply disruption responses, including cross-functional incident leadership and supplier recovery execution. Drive supplier cost-down and value-engineering initiatives with quantifiable savings and tactical roadmaps tied to production volume forecasts and BOM changes. Own supplier disputes, claims, and contractual compliance; negotiate settlements and corrective remedies to protect Zipline’s operational continuity. What You'll Bring 5+ years of hands-on sourcing, commodity management, or supplier leadership experience supporting high-reliability hardware production (aerospace, defense, robotics, automotive, or medtech). Senior candidates with deeper scale should map experience to specific commodities named above. Proven track record negotiating and managing multi-million-dollar supplier contracts and delivering quantifiable outcomes (e.g., % cost savings, OTD improvement, PPM reduction, ramp throughput achieved). Provide concrete examples in your application. Deep technical familiarity with at least one critical commodity area (electronics assemblies, motors/actuators, batteries, composites, precision machining) and the associated supplier ecosystem and qualification practices. Experience driving supplier qualification and industrialization into volume production under aggressive schedules; comfortable managing frequent engineering changes and rework cycles. Strong analytical skills: should-cost modeling, total-cost-of-ownership, spend segmentation, and supplier risk scoring. Able to produce supplier business cases and defend sourcing decisions to executives. Familiarity with supplier quality systems and regulatory/traceability requirements (AS9100/ISO9001, lot traceability, FAI) where applicable. Must be based in or willing to be full-time onsite at Zipline HQ in South San Francisco; travel 20–30% on supplier/site visits and occasional international trips required. Operates with high ownership: makes decisions with incomplete data, escalates early, and drives supplier accountability through on-site engagement and contractual levers. Major bonuses (not required) Advanced degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, or Business. Prior experience supporting flight-critical systems or battery supply chains at scale. History of executing localization or vertical integration programs and managing complex global supplier portfolios. description: We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters. Ford’s Electric Vehicles, Digital and Design (EVDD) team is charged with delivering the company’s vision of a fully electric transportation future. EVDD is customer-obsessed, entrepreneurial, and data-driven and is dedicated to delivering industry-leading customer experience for electric vehicle buyers and owners. You’ll join an agile team of doers pioneering our EV future by working collaboratively, staying focused on only what matters, and delivering excellence day in and day out. Join us to make positive change by helping build a better world where every person is free to move and pursue their dreams. In this position... The global supply chain behind UEV must be as innovative as the platform itself. As Global Supply Manager, you’ll own the end-to-end sourcing strategy for critical vehicle spend. You’ll partner with engineering from concept through launch, using first-principles decision-making to deliver breakthrough outcomes. You will lead global supplier negotiations and structure commercial agreements that protect program timing without sacrificing cost leverage. You’ll also play a central role in one of the most complex challenges facing the industry today: designing a supply chain that is resilient to geopolitical risk and compliant with a rapidly evolving global trade and tariff environment. What you'll do... Own end-to-end sourcing strategy for critical spend areas across the UEV platform and follow-on advanced EV programs from sourcing strategy development through SOP, including supplier selection, contracting, and ongoing cost, quality, and delivery performance. Partner with engineering from concept through launch to align sourcing strategy with technical roadmaps, design freeze milestones, and prototype-to-production transitions. Structure commercial agreements that protect program timing without ceding cost leverage. Build first-principles should-cost models with cross-functional teams to drive a ground-up, physics-based part and system cost perspective. Use these models to set negotiation positions, evaluate quote submissions, and challenge supplier pricing line by line. Lead make-vs-buy analysis to ensure we have a best-in-class supply chain that delivers optimal value. Develop the supply base for resilience. Identify and qualify Tier 1 and Tier 2 partners across geographies; build dual-source and regional capacity strategies that address raw material scarcity, geopolitical risk, and an evolving global trade and tariff environment. Drive automation across the supply chain to deliver best-in-class supply chain efficiency. Partner with suppliers to identify opportunities for process automation and robotics. Shape the tools and processes the ADVEV supply chain runs on, including should-cost methodology, supplier and agreement management systems, and AI-enabled analytics that scale how Ford evaluates suppliers, parts, and agreements. You'll have... Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Business, Supply Chain, Operations Management or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. 5+ years of experience in supply chain management or commodity management. Experience bringing creative negotiation skills and out-of-the-box strategy. Strong relationship management skills with internal and external stakeholders. Even better, you may have... Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, Supply Chain, or related field, or MBA. Hands-on experience building and launching highly effective supply chains. Strong written and verbal communication skills. An eagerness to work cross-functionally in a dynamic environment where you are part of a high performing team. A systems approach to design and development with the desire and curiosity to strive for exceptional delivery execution and continuous improvement. Eagerness to expand into new commodity areas as the ADVEV portfolio grows. You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply! As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including: Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, new parent ramp-up programs, subsidized back-up child care and more Family building benefits including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and more Vehicle discount program for employees and family members and management leases Tuition assistance Established and active employee resource groups Paid time off for individual and team community service A generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day Paid time off and the option to purchase additional vacation time. This position is a salary grade 8 and ranges from $109,100-$182,800. For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/LL6 Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value. Visa sponsorship is available for this position. Candidates for positions with Ford Motor Company must be legally authorized to work in the United States. In the United States, if you need a reasonable accommodation for the online application process due to a disability, please call 1-888-336-0660. description: Join the team bringing advanced autonomy to the built world At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world.
