description: Description Application deadline: Oct 7, 2026 Today, Amazon Web Services provides a highly reliable, scalable, low cost infrastructure platform in the cloud that powers hundreds of thousands of businesses in 190 countries around the world. The AWS Cloud infrastructure is built around Regions and Availability Zones. AWS Regions provide multiple, physically separated and isolated Availability Zones connected with low latency, high throughput, and highly redundant networking. The connectivity and fiber materials that go into those connections decide how fast and how reliably we build. Would you like to join the team that sources and qualifies the materials behind that low latency, high throughput, and highly redundant network? Amazon Web Services is looking for a highly motivated, technically savvy Material Supply Chain Manager to develop and scale the connectivity and fiber material supply behind one of the world's largest and most complex networks. You own the strategy for a material category as a business, and you carry the commercial and technical relationship with the suppliers in that category. You define the sourcing strategy, lead the negotiations, and secure the supply we need to hit tight build schedules across regions. You work in a space where the business problem, the domain strategy, and the technical solution are often undefined, and you bring clarity and deliver independently. You lead the commercial engagements that drive the strategy, including originating and negotiating new contract structures with suppliers rather than executing terms someone else set. You partner with legal and finance to define the financial and legal guardrails for a deal, then assess contract terms against those guardrails on your own judgment. You shape the roadmap for next generation fiber and connectors, and you qualify those materials with engineering so we build faster and at lower cost. Your scope reaches across orgs and geographies. You influence the vendors, legal, finance, design engineering, and program teams who own infrastructure delivery, and you drive strategic decisions that affect build plans in multiple regions. You translate deployment demand into a supply plan, remove single source risks, and bring new suppliers online to protect our schedules and cost targets. You write the narratives that carry these decisions, and you present them to senior managers and directors. You will be part of a creative, efficient team tasked with tackling the most interesting and challenging problems in connectivity and fiber materials. Our networks lead the industry in capacity and cost effectiveness, and the materials strategy behind them keeps that lead. You will stay at the forefront of the material development industry and deliver the most innovative material solutions to our programs. You will succeed in this role if you enjoy owning a category end to end, moving between a supplier negotiation and a technical qualification review in the same day, and making decisions with incomplete data under real schedule pressure. You set the strategy, then drive it to results. This role requires travel of 25 - 50% Key job responsibilities You own the supply chain strategy for a defined connectivity and fiber material category and carry the commercial relationship with the suppliers in that category. You build the demand forecast and supply plan that keeps programs on schedule, translating deployment demand into a clear view of what materials we need, when, and in what volume across regions. You define the strategy and execute it, usually within broader guidance. You originate and negotiate new contract structures, pricing, capacity commitments, and supply terms, then manage supplier performance against those terms. You partner with legal and finance to set acceptable financial and legal guardrails, and you assess contract terms against those guardrails independently. You lead the qualification of new suppliers and new materials with engineering. You identify supply risks early, build mitigation plans, and report category health to senior managers and directors through clear narratives and metrics. You drive cost reduction and dual sourcing initiatives that improve resilience across the network, and you mentor others on the team. About The Team Global Connectivity Infrastructure Development - Fiber Deployment plans, manages, and delivers the physical fiber network that connects AWS data centers. The high-volume metro team delivers the fiber that brings new AWS capacity online across our busiest metro markets. You will work alongside construction vendors, engineers, and the internal customers who depend on that capacity, building large-scale fiber networks on time and to a high quality bar. Our focus for the coming years is scaling delivery without losing that quality, and this role is central to it. New teammates reach independent project ownership quickly, supported by runbooks and mentorship. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. description: Position Summary The Sourcing Specialist will support in the development and implementation of commodity / supply chain activities that significantly contributes to year over year sales growth and operational improvement through Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) sourcing process. Visit suppliers for continuous improvement and project execution in partnership with the Strategic Sourcing Manager. Understanding of procurement category management with strong understanding on cost reduction, procurement market and supplier strategy, risk mitigation and contracts setting. Basic understanding of commodity markets in a global supply chain environment: steel, aluminum, copper, plastics, paper etc. Desired prior experience of working within a global team and global category management setting. Strong project management experience: able to independently drive new supplier sourcing and or cost reduction initiatives and meet key sourcing objectives in a timely manner under the direction of a Strategic Sourcing Manager. Knowledge of basic manufacturing processes, metal cutting, casting, machining, plastic injection molding, metal fabrication, and electronics. Demonstrated experience reading engineering drawings and specifications will be an advantage. Basic experience in global and comprehensive supplier relationship management and advanced negotiation techniques. Data analysis, problem solving and reporting skill sets. Experience working in global supply environment and with international suppliers or colleagues. Demonstrated teamwork skills, self-motivated and strong communication and interpersonal skills. Knowledge of Quality Management Systems, ISO and 6-sigma disciplines, training and experience will be an advantage. Working knowledge of ERP systems such as Oracle, QAD, Fourth Shift etc will be an advantage. Health Savings Account: Benefit from annual employer contributions to your HSA. Safe Work Environment: Work in a clean and safe environment. Generous Paid Time Off: Enjoy 14 paid holidays, including a holiday shutdown between Christmas and New Year’s, plus paid vacation available from day one. Paid Parental Leave: Take advantage of paid parental leave to support your family.

description: Company Overview Sarmal, Inc. is a San Diego–based biotechnology company developing next-generation genomics and molecular detection platforms. description: Description Position Summary This role owns procurement execution for all non-OEM (non-Caterpillar) supplier commodities supporting MacAllister's electric power strategic accounts business. Conduct market analysis, supplier benchmarking, and total cost of ownership (TCO) evaluations for assigned categories. Identify and qualify new suppliers, including second-source options for supply risk mitigation. Lead supplier RFQ/RFP processes, evaluate supplier proposals, and recommend supplier selection decisions. Maintain an approved supplier list for assigned categories in coordination with Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE). Identify and execute cost savings, cost avoidance, and supplier optimization opportunities. Note: Supplier quality performance (conformance, audits, NCRs, corrective actions) is owned by the Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) function. Monitor supplier capacity constraints, material lead times, and market conditions affecting assigned categories. Escalate unresolved supply disruptions or delivery risks to Supply Chain Management with proposed mitigation actions. Maintain awareness of industry trends relevant to data center power infrastructure procurement. Coordinate with Project Management to align procurement timelines with project delivery schedules. Coordinate with Supplier Quality Engineering on supplier qualification, quality performance issues, and corrective action requirements. Coordinate with Field Execution to ensure material availability supports commissioning readiness. Communicate procurement status, risks, and supply constraints to internal stakeholders. Strong communication and stakeholder alignment skills across technical and operational teams. Ability to operate independently and manage ambiguity in a scaling organization. This role will help drive strategic sourcing, supplier management, contract review, cost optimization, and procurement governance across a broad range of indirect spend categories. Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To Lead sourcing activities across multiple indirect spend categories, including professional services, facilities, office services, marketing, HR-related services, financial services, business operations, travel, supplies, and other business services. Support supplier selection, onboarding, performance management, renewal reviews, and vendor rationalization efforts. Negotiate supplier pricing, service levels, commercial terms, and contract protections in partnership with business owners, Legal, Finance, and other stakeholders. Review supplier agreements before Legal review to confirm business terms, pricing, service requirements, renewal language, approvals, and procurement documentation are complete and accurate. Identify opportunities to reduce cost, consolidate spend, standardize buying channels, improve supplier value, and strengthen procurement compliance. Maintain sourcing documentation, supplier records, approval history, savings tracking, and other procurement materials to support governance and audit readiness. Contribute to procurement process improvements, tools, templates, workflows, reporting, and automation initiatives. Your Experience. Experience supporting sourcing events, supplier evaluations, pricing analysis, contract negotiations, and vendor management across multiple indirect spend categories. Strong understanding of procurement best practices, contract review, supplier governance, cost analysis, and stakeholder management. Ability to analyze spend data, supplier proposals, pricing models, total cost of ownership, and business impacts. Strong communication, negotiation, organization, and project management skills. Preferred Qualifications Procurement or supply chain certification such as CPSM, CSCP, CPM, CPP, or similar. Experience in professional services, financial services, tax, audit, advisory, or business services environments. Familiarity with procurement, ERP, contract management, or workflow tools such as SAP, Coupa, Oracle, Workday, Ariba, or similar platforms. Experience developing sourcing templates, vendor scorecards, savings trackers, procurement policies, or supplier governance models. Key Competencies Strategic sourcing and category support Vendor management and supplier performance Contract and commercial review Cost analysis and value delivery Stakeholder partnership and communication Procurement governance and compliance Process improvement and change support Demonstrated experience in the financial services, tax, audit, or advisory sectors is highly desirable. description: Onsite: Savannah, GA At Gulfstream, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We believe in inspiring and empowering every individual to reach their fullest potential. From workforce development and meaningful connections to a culture of trust, respect, and integrity, we invest in our employees so they can do their best work and achieve success together. Creating and delivering the world’s finest aviation experience starts with our people—and when our people thrive, so does our mission. Join a high-impact procurement team supporting systems and composites, including lighting, landing gear, hardware, and chemicals. In this senior-level role, you will lead complex sourcing initiatives, influence supplier strategy, and mentor procurement professionals while driving performance across critical aerospace programs. What You Will Do Lead complex procurement projects, including negotiations for high-value aerospace components, systems, and services Develop and execute strategic sourcing initiatives to drive cost savings, performance, and supply continuity Evaluate supplier proposals, conduct bid analysis, and negotiate pricing, schedules, and contract terms Establish and manage long-term agreements (e.g., Master Orders, Blanket Purchase Agreements) Develop and manage supplier performance plans, including quality, delivery, and reliability metrics Identify and resolve supplier and internal performance issues through corrective action and cross-functional coordination Serve as a primary point of contact for internal stakeholders on strategic commodities Lead, mentor, and support procurement team members to achieve departmental and program objectives Collaborate with Engineering, Program Management, and Operations to align procurement strategies with program goals Ensure compliance with preferred Demonstrated experience negotiating and managing high-value, complex, multi-year procurements Strong knowledge of contract law, procurement regulations, and industry best practices Experience managing supplier performance and strategic supplier relationships Proven leadership ability with experience mentoring or guiding team members Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills Proficiency in SAP or equivalent ERP systems preferred Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills Additional Information A credit history check from a This position is on-site in Savannah, GA Apply Now If you’re ready to take your procurement leadership to the next level and make a meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply. At Gulfstream, you’ll be part of a team dedicated to innovation, excellence, and delivering the world’s finest aviation experience. Education And Experience Requirements Bachelor's Degree in supply chain, business administration or related field required or equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Master's Degree preferred. 5 years procurement, supply chain or related technical experience. Position Purpose Develops, plans and leads complex procurement projects including negotiations for contract awards and resolution involving high-value aerospace components, systems, and services. Coordinates cross-functional teams, manages supplier relationships, and ensures compliance with industry standards and program requirements. Oversees procurement planning, execution, and performance monitoring to support strategic business objectives. Responsible for preparing annual supplier performance master plan including objectives and priorities for material management, quality, reliability and product support as well as calendar and format for program reviews . Manage supplier performance to master plan by identifying problems, both internally and at the supplier, determining source of the problem, taking corrective action, and planning and coordinating the involvement of Gulfstream Management, as appropriate . Interpret program and/or statement of work requirements; recommends and implements action with suppliers Purchasing/Materials Manager to ensure achievement of all requirements . Support continuous improvement initiatives within the procurement function . description: CULTIVATE A BETTER WORLD Food served fast does not have to be a typical fast-food experience. Chipotle has always done things differently, both in and out of our restaurants. This role serves as the raw material procurement lead for applicable categories, and a key partner to Planning, Commercialization, Culinary, Marketing, FSQA, Finance, commissary manufacturers, and ingredient suppliers. The Senior Analyst, Commissary Ingredient Procurement will independently manage ingredient supplier relationships, sourcing events, ingredient cost models, item setup, pricing, raw material tracking, and inventory risk. A critical responsibility is owning the end-to-end raw material lifecycle for sauce and seasoning ingredients related to Limited Time Offers (LTOs), from forecast and sourcing through purchasing visibility, consumption, reconciliation, and program closeout, ensuring materials are available in the right quantity and at the right time while eliminating shortages, avoiding excess inventory, and minimizing financial exposure. You will also maintain and update policies and procedures to ensure procurement activities are in accordance with corporate standards. Build and independently manage ingredient supplier relationships to support service, quality, supply continuity, capacity, cost, and innovation objectives. Lead RFI, RFQ, and RFP activities for confirmed raw materials, including supplier outreach, bid analysis, commercial recommendations, and implementation support. Create and maintain raw material item setup documentation, SKU creation, pricing records, sourcing information, units of measure, and product attributes within Oracle and other procurement systems. Develop, maintain, and analyze ingredient and raw material cost models, commodity inputs, supplier quotations, market information, and forecasted financial impacts to support sourcing and negotiation decisions. Partner with Commercialization, Culinary, Marketing, FSQA, Planning, and commissary manufacturers to ensure raw materials are sourced, qualified, contracted, and available before trials, training, and launch. Own raw material tracking for LTO programs, including analyzing raw material inputs and financials, communicating raw material risk, monitoring supplier lead times, production usage, yield inputs, shelf life, and projected shortage or excess exposure. Recommend changes to raw material commitments, including splitting, reducing, deferring, reallocating, or canceling orders, and escalate decisions that exceed delegated authority. Maintain ingredient mapping by SKU, supplier, source, lead time, contract status, capacity, risk, and approved alternate or backup supply options. Support and lead routine raw material pricing negotiations and support strategic or high-value negotiations with the Senior Manager, Commissary. Monitor supplier performance, contract utilization, pricing compliance, on-time delivery, corrective actions, and capacity commitments; prepare inputs for supplier reviews and QBRs. Identify and deliver cost savings, cost avoidance, supply assurance, and process improvement opportunities without compromising food safety, quality, or service. Working knowledge of strategic sourcing, RFIs, RFQs, RFPs, supplier negotiations, contracts, commodity or ingredient cost drivers, and supplier performance management. Ability to independently identify supply risks, quantify operational and financial impact, develop recommendations, and communicate escalations clearly. Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple internal stakeholders, suppliers, materials, and LTO timelines simultaneously. Experience partnering cross-functionally with Planning, Commercialization, Culinary, Marketing, FSQA, Finance, Operations, and external suppliers. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to coordinate activities with suppliers and internal teams. Experience supporting sourcing activities, supplier management, inventory planning, or commercialization projects preferred. description: Beehive Industries is dedicated to Powering American Defense by revolutionizing the design, development, and delivery of jet propulsion systems to support the warfighter. Through the integration of additive manufacturing, the company aims to meet the growing and urgent needs for unmanned aerial defense by dramatically improving a jet engine’s speed to market, fuel efficiency, and cost. Founded in 2020, the company is headquartered in Centennial, Colorado, with additional facilities in Knoxville, Tennessee, Loveland Ohio, and Mount Vernon, Ohio. Beehive is committed to grow and advance the defense industrial base while manufacturing exclusively in the USA. This role will be located at our Cincinnati, Ohio facility. Role Overview We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Buyer to own and support execution of all outside processing and special process requirements in a fast-paced aerospace and defense environment. This role owns the supplier relationship and purchasing process for outside services including non-destructive testing, heat treatment, and other specialized manufacturing services The Buyer works closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Supply Planning, and Program teams to ensure outside processing is completed in accordance with purchase order requirements, customer specifications, applicable aerospace standards, and required delivery schedules. This position is responsible for negotiating long term agreements, understanding supplier capacity and constraints, partnering with technical teams to qualify new sources and managing the complete outside-service process from purchase requisition through supplier execution. What You’ll Do... Manage purchase orders and supplier relationships for all assigned outside processing and special process requirements. Manage RFQs/RFPs, supplier selection, bid analysis, negotiations, and contract execution. Ensure full compliance with FAR/DFARS requirements and all government contracting regulations throughout the procurement process. Collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Quality, Finance, and Program Management teams to support business objectives. Negotiate pricing, payment terms, lead times, service agreements, and long-term supply arrangements. Develop and maintain supplier relationships to ensure performance in quality, delivery, cost, and responsiveness. Identify and execute cost reduction, process improvement, and supply chain risk mitigation initiatives. Maintain accurate procurement records, purchase orders, and sourcing documentation within ERP/MRP systems. Support audits and documentation requirements related to AS9100, ISO standards, and government contracting compliance. Own supplier delivery performance for outside processing requirements and proactively manage material through the supplier network. Coordinate shipment of material to and from outside processors to support production schedules. Monitor supplier lead times, work-in-process, capacity constraints, and potential delivery risks. Support long-term agreements, pricing agreements, blanket purchase orders, and other commercial strategies where appropriate You have... Education Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or related field preferred. Experience 3–7+ years of purchasing or procurement experience in manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or highly regulated industries. Skills & Competencies Demonstrated experience preparing, managing, and auditing procurement compliance documentation. Strong negotiation, analytical, and supplier management skills. Working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems Ability to read and interpret statements of work, and technical specifications Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and procurement analytics. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment. The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance Nice to have... Experience in aerospace, defense, precision machining, additive, or advanced manufacturing environments. Experience supporting lean manufacturing or continuous improvement initiatives. Experience with long-term supply agreements and logistics Experience with ERP/MRP systems such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or similar. If this sounds like you, please submit an application with your resume. This could be the opportunity you are looking for to expand your skills, contribute to a winning team, and work with talented people who love what they do and take pride in our mission. Beehive Industries offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes group Medical, Dental, Life, and Short and Long-Term disability coverage from day one. We also offer a generous 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan with a Company match. Every role at Beehive Industries is bonus eligible and will also receive equity in the company. Beehive Industries is committed to full compliance with applicable anti-discrimination laws. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We strive to create an inclusive work environment and will not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Req ID: 1536 FLSA Status: Exempt Pay Range: $71,304 - $110,000 Salary Is Based On Experience, Skills, And Education This position is 100% onsite The Marvin Group is a Strategic Partner for Global Alternate Mission Equipment and Sustainment The Marvin Group, a leading defense contractor, plays a crucial role in the development and manufacturing of various systems for military aerospace and vehicles. Based in Southern California near the Los Angeles International Airport, The Marvin Group consists of Marvin Engineering (MEC), Marvin Test Solutions (MTS) and Marvin Land Systems (MLS). Marvin Engineering designs and produces military Alternate Mission Equipment. Marvin Test Solutions designs and manufactures armament Test Equipment. Marvin Land Systems specializes in the design and build of power and thermal management systems. Our collaboration extends across a diverse array of programs and platforms, including major military prime contractors such as Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, and Raytheon. POSITION SUMMARY: Buyer IV supports Indirect Procurement and is responsible for purchases that support day-to-day operations (instead of direct material purchases for production). Indirect Procurement means the purchase of software licenses, IT infrastructure, travel, construction, leases, a wide variety of services (temps, maintenance, landscaping, cafeteria, company benefits, etc.) and capital equipment (usually large machining or quality measurement equipment but could include things like forklifts or other vehicles). These are things we need to buy that do not go into the products we manufacture. This role ensures these “indirect” items are procured efficiently, cost-effectively, and in compliance with organizational and regulatory standards. Robust negotiation, independent problem-solving, the ability to work through ambiguity to develop solutions, and clear and concise communication are all critical for this role. Marvin Engineering is growing, and our indirect procurement team needs to develop processes and expertise in all of the areas described above. The successful candidate will already have robust experience in most, if not all, of these areas. We want to leverage this experience to enable fast expansion while utilizing best practices in the industry. Draft and ensure approvals of purchase orders. Ensure appropriate review and negotiate contracts for indirect procurement. Strong experience with PowerPoint Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal. Experience using purchasing software. Collaborative with cross-functional customers Sound business decisions and common sense. Ability to work well under pressure and meet deadlines. Ability to communicate with General Contractors. description: Eaton’s ES AMER ARS PDCAD division is currently seeking a Senior Buyer. This position is onsite, Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm, at our Arden, NC Eaton facility. The Senior Buyer supports Eaton’s supply chain purchasing department through the effective procurement of a wide variety of direct material from domestic and global sources ensuring that quality, delivery, and specification requirements are met at the lowest possible total cost. This individual will take leadership of cost reduction projects, commercial negotiations, and implementation of sourcing strategies. Additionally, this individual will be expected to identify, improve, and implement business processes as well as provide leadership within the department and with the supply base. This position requires the ability to develop a competitive environment within the supply base and to make sourcing decisions based on total cost of ownership considerations. The expected annual salary range for this role is $86000 - $126000 a year. Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations. What You’ll Do Initiates quoting activity, evaluates supplier proposals, and negotiates price and delivery based on total cost of ownership and ensuring strategic alignment with corporate and local goals and objectives. Lead commercial negotiations with suppliers seeking mutually beneficial long-term relationships. Work with design engineering groups across multiple product lines, to ensure successful, on time development and launch of new products, by identifying the optimal sourcing strategies. Works with the material planning group to drive supply base to meet delivery and inventory requirements. Lead by example in the tasks required to meet departmental requirements. Assist in the training and development of personnel within the department. Acts as a conduit between suppliers and Eaton personnel to resolve quality and / or technical issues as they arise. Lead supplier management and development activities driving continuous improvement in Eaton’s metrics and Talenthub goals. Research new sources of supply and performs tactical Supply Chain assessments of these sources, including the development of supplier selection criteria. Facilitate the implementation of goals and objectives between Corporate commodity management and the facility SCM team. Leverage relationships to hold suppliers accountable to perform to Eaton’s expectations on delivery, quality and overall cost. Maintains all records and correspondence relative to quotations, purchase orders, contracts, and agreements. Proactively resolve supplier accounts payable issues. Participate in cross-functional teams chartered with improving supplier performance and executing corrective actions and drive continuous improvement through the supply base with a focus on cost, quality, on-time-performance and inventory DOH. Qualifications Basic Qualifications: Must meet one of the following: A Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution OR an Associates Degree AND a minimum of 7 years of experience in a supply chain/purchasing environment. Minimum of 3 years of supply chain experience in manufacturing industry or operations environment. Minimum of 3 years of experience with direct buying within a manufacturing, operations, or supply chain environment. No relocation is offered. Candidates must currently reside within a 50-mile radius of Arden, NC to be considered. Active-Duty Military are exempt from this geographical limitation. Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc. Preferred Qualifications MBA or advanced Master's degree from an accredited institution. CPIM, CPM or similar professional certifications. Demonstrated experience in strategic purchasing and sourcing within a manufacturing or supply chain environment. Skills Broad understanding of supply chain principles and the ability to interpret and communicate complex specifications and instructions. Thorough understanding of negotiation techniques and tactics Self-directed, self-starter with exceptional negotiating skills, excellent communication (verbal and written) and interpersonal skills are required. Demonstrated proficiency in the use of personal computers and strong knowledge of Microsoft Office. Thorough knowledge of purchasing and principles including the ability to research, analyze negotiate and close various types of purchase efforts within guidelines of good business and ethical practices. Possessing the following leadership characteristics: handling ambiguity; flexibility; integrity; leading change; learning agility; strategic agility; and vision. Assuring a timely delivery of quality raw materials and components requires the proper choice of vendors and continual communications with vendor of choice. Maintaining consistent pricing and cost improvement required the creativity of product review, new vendor search, department interface or redesign and the ability to negotiate needed price. Responding to all levels of managerial requests requires flexibility of dealing with new situations and demands while maintaining normal activities. Operating within the confines of a receipt budget while balancing the requirements of manufacturing and need to control inventory investment. Providing leadership and informing various members of total organization while their individual interest is not in conformance with materials. Planning the timely acquisition of quality materials to assure the smooth flow of manufacturing, while maintaining minimum inventory investment and improving costs. Demonstrated success in materials, purchasing, or customer support activities. We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law. Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws. You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report. To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number. We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. description: About Blue Bird Corporation Blue Bird (NASDAQ: BLBD) is recognized as a technology leader and innovator of school buses since its founding in 1927. Our dedicated team members design, engineer and manufacture school buses with a singular focus on safety, reliability, and durability. School buses carry the most precious cargo in the world – 25 million children twice a day – making them the most trusted mode of student transportation. The company is the proven leader in low- and zero-emission school buses with more than 25,000 propane, natural gas, and electric powered buses sold. Blue Bird is transforming the student transportation industry through cleaner energy solutions. For more information on Blue Bird’s complete product and service portfolio, visit www.blue-bird.com. JOB SUMMARY: Reporting to the Senior Manager, Purchasing, the Senior Buyer, Powertrain & Chassis Systems is responsible for leading the strategic sourcing, contract negotiation, and operational lifecycle management for powertrain, chassis, and assigned heavy mechanical and structural commodities. This role serves as the primary commercial and operational owner for critical components and systems, including engine and powertrain systems, transmissions and driveline, steering, braking, suspension, axles, wheels and tires, and assigned structural/mechanical systems. The position balances long-term cost optimization and supplier relationship management with aggressive hands-on risk mitigation, serving as the ultimate escalation point for production shortages, supplier recovery, and supply continuity planning to ensure uninterrupted vehicle assembly. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Commodity Strategy & Sourcing: Develop and execute comprehensive sourcing strategies for the Powertrain & Chassis Systems portfolio to optimize total cost of ownership (TCO), quality, and delivery. Supplier Risk & Crisis Management: Lead operational risk management, serve as the primary escalation point for critical chassis component shortages, and establish cross-functional crisis management teams to resolve supplier delivery failures. Contract & Cost Negotiation: Lead multi-million-dollar contract negotiations, long-term agreements (LTAs), and pricing reviews with major tier-1 automotive and heavy-duty commercial vehicle suppliers. Supplier Performance & Technical Recovery: Monitor On-Time Delivery (OTD) and quality governance; lead 8D root-cause investigations and corrective action plans directly with supplier manufacturing plants when quality or delivery targets are missing. Capacity & Vulnerability Mapping: Conduct regular supplier capacity reviews, tooling and manufacturing assessments, sub-tier dependency reviews, and vulnerability mapping to identify capacity constraints, long-lead components, and other supply continuity risks. Program Launch & Supplier Transition: Lead purchasing activities supporting new product introduction and supplier transition, including sourcing readiness, commercial closure, tooling, capacity validation, APQP/PPAP execution, early supplier engagement (ESI), and production launch readiness. Resilience Planning: Drive dual-sourcing and manufacturing contingency initiatives for high-risk, single-sourced components and systems. Operational Discipline: Develop KPI dashboards, manage material cost variance reporting, and mentor junior buyers and operational specialists within the purchasing team. REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES: Strong knowledge of automotive or commercial vehicle powertrain, chassis, driveline, and/or heavy mechanical systems. Advanced Sourcing & Negotiation: Proven track record of managing high-spend portfolios, executing complex supplier agreements, and navigating raw material (steel/aluminum) indexing. Operational Recovery: Demonstrated experience leading supplier recovery efforts and managing business continuity in high-pressure manufacturing environments. Quality & Engineering Literacy: Strong understanding of automotive quality standards, APQP, PPAP, blueprint reading, and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T). Influence & Collaboration: Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders (Engineering, Quality, Operations) without direct authority. Systems Proficiency: High proficiency in ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle, or Infor) and advanced Microsoft Excel data analysis capabilities. EDUCATION AND EXPEREINCE Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Operations Management, or related field 7+ years of supply chain, purchasing, operations, planning, or supplier management experience 3+ years of strategic sourcing, commodity management, supplier management, or purchasing experience within automotive, commercial vehicle, heavy truck, aerospace, or similar complex manufacturing environments; powertrain or chassis commodity experience preferred. 3+ years leading projects, crisis management initiatives, or operational teams Manufacturing experience required Must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident Preferred Education And Experience MBA preferred Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt preferred APICS/ASCM certification preferred PMP certification preferred Experience leading supply chain transformation initiatives Experience supporting executive leadership reviews Automotive or commercial vehicle experience strongly preferred WE VALUE Strategic thinking with operational execution capability Leadership during crisis situations Ability to influence and build relationships Strong analytical skills Continuous improvement mindset Strong customer and production support focus INCLUDES Continued Professional Development Benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, 14 paid holidays, vacation time and 401k matching WORK CONDITIONS The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Local travel 30% Office environment and production environment Must work in manufacturing environment with exposure to heat, cold and noise Fast paced production area with moving objects and sheet metal Occasional periods of standing or sitting for extended periods of time Must wear appropriate PPE when and where required Frequent weeks working 40+ hours Frequent communication with people throughout the day The specific statements shown in each section of this description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria necessary to successfully perform the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions Blue Bird® is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. We strive to have the best available talent in every job based on the Knowledge, Skills and Abilities each person brings. Blue Bird is committed to compliance with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. This commitment applies to all persons involved in Company operations and prohibits unlawful discrimination in all forms. All candidates must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility at the time of hire.

description: At DuPont, our purpose is to empower the world with essential innovations to thrive. We work on things that matter. Whether it’s providing clean water to more than a billion people on the planet, producing materials that are essential in everyday technology devices from smartphones to electric vehicles, or protecting workers around the world. Discover the many reasons the world’s most talented people are choosing to work at DuPont. Why Join Us | DuPont Careers Do you like being involved in major projects from the start and turning complex commercial work into real business value? DuPont's Global Procurement team is looking for a Senior Project Buyer – Operating Materials & Services to lead procurement for capital and operational projects across the company. This is a visible role with real influence. You'll be the main procurement contact for capital and site teams and represent the team to internal business groups. You'll also guide other project buyers and work closely with the commodity buy team. Your sourcing, contracting and negotiating will directly affect project cost, schedule and success. What You'll Do Shape sourcing strategy from the start Build and carry out sourcing strategies that fit each project's scope, schedule and budget. Get involved early in the project lifecycle to shape procurement and contracting decisions. Assign projects to other buyers based on buy type and team workload. Lead high-value sourcing and contracting Run the full sourcing process for major packages: RFI/RFP/RFQ, technical and commercial bid evaluation, and award. Structure and negotiate complex contracts (lump-sum, reimbursable, unit-rate and hybrid), balancing risk and value. Design contracting strategies that fit each project's risk profile and current market conditions. Negotiate and deliver measurable value Negotiate pricing, payment milestones, warranties, liquidated damages, retention and performance guarantees. Drive cost savings, cost avoidance and value engineering without compromising safety, quality or schedule. Manage currency, escalation and commodity-linked pricing on long-duration contracts. Build strong supplier and contractor partnerships With the commodity buy team, qualify, evaluate and manage OEMs, fabricators, EPC contractors and engineering firms. Manage supplier performance through expediting, inspection and progress monitoring until delivery. Manage risk and governance Find and reduce schedule, quality, financial and single-source risks on the critical path. Ensure compliance with capital approval (AFE) processes, delegation of authority, safety rules and regulatory standards. Work Across Functions And Keep Leaders Informed Work with Engineering, Business, Legal, Finance and Operations to keep procurement in step with project milestones. Prepare executive-ready updates on capital commitments, savings, cash flow and procurement risk using Power BI and Excel. Support project audits, cost forecasting and closeout. What You Bring Education and experience Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business or a related technical field 5+ years of procurement experience CPSM and/or PMP certification preferred Skills And Strengths Hands-on experience with complex RFx processes, market analysis and creating business value A track record of developing, implementing and managing complex contracts Advanced negotiation skills and strong commercial judgment The ability to communicate clearly and influence people without direct authority The ability to manage several priorities in a fast-moving project environment High ethical standards Join our Talent Community to stay connected with us! DuPont is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation to search or apply for a position, please visit our Accessibility Page for Contact Information. DuPont offers a comprehensive pay and benefits package. To learn more visit the Compensation and Benefits page. The Pay range for this role is $81,900.00 - $128,700.00 Annual How Base Pay is Determined: DuPont has job leveling frameworks that help organize roles based on progressive levels of responsibility, proficiency and qualifications. Each role has an associated pay range (or an established pay rate for some roles) based on the competitive market in each country where we operate. Each individual’s pay is based on a variety of factors, including their role and the associated pay range for that role, their geographic location (i.e., country, state, metropolitan area), as well as their skills, experience, education and certifications, and performance.

description: Status: Exempt Department: Purchasing/Supply Chain Position Summary The Sr. Buyer serves a critical role to Plug Power by working to procure necessary parts and components in support of the manufacturing operation while also acting as a lead resource for the rest of the purchasing team. The Sr. Buyer role must establish very strong and mutually beneficial relationships with suppliers and therefore requires dynamic interpersonal skills. A most successful Sr. Buyer exhibits timely and accurate transactional work, exceptional cross-functional collaboration, hands-on communication skills, and untiring follow-up to ensure completion of critical tasks and projects. The ideal candidate is able to self-manage projects and company initiatives with limited direction required from management. This individual may be involved in negotiating short- and long-term agreements, incorporating strategic purchasing initiatives, developing and implementing procurement strategies. Additionally, the Sr. Buyer will be looked to as a purchasing team lead and will service as an advisor and mentor to other purchasing staff. Core Duties And Responsibilities Perform transactional duties including placing of purchase orders to procure material in support of manufacturing and other business functions Build and maintain effective cross-functional relationships; communicate regularly to maintain an understanding of timelines and activities which impact supply chain Act as a primary partner to the manufacturing operation by understanding build schedules and managing supply chain activities to increase efficiency and eliminate downtime Take responsibility for accurate and on-time delivery of parts and components; follow-up on PO’s with suppliers and manage delivery date expectations as necessary with all relevant stakeholders Understand material specifications and quality metrics affecting assigned parts and components; work collaboratively to resolve quality issues with suppliers Develop strong relationships with suppliers and communicate regularly; manage date pull-ins and push-outs on an ongoing basis Serve as a mentor and advisor to the purchasing team, guiding and directing activities of fellow Buyers as needed Train new team members, acting as advisor and resource Leverage positive working relationships with suppliers based upon mutual benefit; seek favorable terms and conditions which positively impact pricing, quality, payment terms, and others as applicable Track supplier performance and provide regular feedback to relevant stakeholders; set clear expectations with suppliers and work to add/replace suppliers as needed for optimal business results Collaborate with colleagues in the finance department to resolve supplier payment issues Represent Plug Power in a professional manner at all times and in all interactions Perform all other duties as assigned Education And Experience Bachelors degree in Engineering, Business, or other applicable field of study and five (5) or more years of related work experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience Experience within a technology manufacturing environment is highly preferred Must be capable of working independently, in a fast-paced environment, with minimal supervision Demonstrated analytical abilities with strong attention to detail Superior communication skills Proficient with Microsoft Office software including highly developed skills within Excel Ability to manage projects and multi-task effectively Ability to role model high standards of professionalism Excellent follow-through Must be driven and self-motivated Must possess the highest ethical standards and a supreme commitment to quality Exempt employees are expected to work as many hours as is necessary to complete their job responsibilities. This may require they work more than eight hours a day and more than five days or 40 hours per week. Plug Power, Inc. is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other legally protected status.

description: Supply Chain Expert – Sourcing & Procurement Location: Dearborn, MI (Day-1 Onsite) Years of Experience: 10–15 Years Job Summary: We are seeking a highly experienced Supply Chain Expert / Subject Matter Expert with deep expertise in sourcing and procurement, vendor management, and end-to-end Source-to-Pay (S2P) processes within the automotive industry. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret spend, supplier, contract, purchase-order, invoice, and performance data. Excellent communication, consulting, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence senior business and functional leaders. Knowledge of automotive procurement practices, supplier quality requirements, regulatory expectations, and global supply-market dynamics. Experience with procurement transformation, shared services, global process ownership, or procurement centre-of-excellence models. Familiarity with data visualization, spend analytics, workflow automation, AI-enabled procurement, and supplier-risk intelligence tools. Experience working with global, cross-functional, and multicultural teams. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Finance, Operations, or a related field; a Master’s degree is preferred and added advantage. 10–15 years of relevant experience in sourcing, procurement, supplier management, or procurement transformation, preferably within automotive or manufacturing. Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional S2P improvement or digital-transformation programmes. Relevant certifications such as CPSM, CIPS, CSCP, PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or procurement-platform certifications are an advantage.

job_title: Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager - Supplier Development
description: Your role The Strategic Sourcing role is accountable for developing and executing a sustainable procurement strategy within their assigned commodity area. This includes establishing and managing long‑term agreements and service‑level commitments, optimising and rationalising the supplier base, and ensuring effective supplier onboarding. A key focus of the role is strengthening supply chain resilience by building. As Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager - Supplier Development, you will execute sourcing strategies that secure qualified capacity for production ramp-up and build a competitive, resilient supply base. You will lead supplier selection, negotiation, onboarding, qualification coordination, launch readiness, and performance, with particular focus on new product introduction, dual sourcing, and continuity of supply. This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports. Manager reflects accountability for sourcing strategies, supplier relationships, spend, contracts, risk, and results. What You Will Do Develop category and supplier strategies aligned with growth, NPI, production ramp-up, cost, capacity, quality, and supply-resilience priorities. Lead market analysis, RFIs, RFQs and RFPs, total-cost evaluation, negotiations, supplier selection, awards, and agreements. Assess suppliers for capability, capacity, processes, quality systems, financial health, scalability, compliance, and risk. Coordinate supplier onboarding and qualification across Engineering, Supplier Quality, Operations, Planning, Finance, and other functions, with clear milestones, owners, risks, and escalations. Facilitate product and part qualification, including specifications, samples, tooling, first articles, validation, deviation closure, approvals, and production release. Engineering and Quality own technical requirements, validation decisions, and formal approval; you drive supplier response, timing, commercial readiness, escalation, and completion. Secure capacity and launch readiness through reviews, forecasts, lead-time and flexibility commitments, inventory plans, and commercial agreements. Build dual-source and continuity plans for critical parts and single-source risks, coordinating alternate-source qualification with technical and quality teams. Lead supplier reviews, performance improvement, and recovery plans covering quality, delivery, capacity, cost, compliance, and risk. Deliver savings, cost avoidance, working-capital improvement, productivity, and total-cost benefits without compromising quality or continuity. Develop supplier relationships that improve access to capacity, technology, and innovation while meeting legal, ethical, sustainability, and Atlas Copco requirements. To succeed, you will need Typically 5-8 years of experience in strategic sourcing, category management, supplier development, procurement, or supply chain, preferably in engineered products or manufacturing. Success sourcing, negotiating with, qualifying, onboarding, and ramping suppliers for NPI or production growth. Experience coordinating suppliers and cross-functional teams through qualification and production release. Strong negotiation, contract management, cost analysis, total-cost, supplier-performance, and risk-management capabilities. Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, bills of material, manufacturing processes, and supplier-capability information. Strong communication, influence, judgment, analytical problem-solving, and project leadership without formal authority. Bachelor's degree in supply chain, engineering, business, operations, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Location and travel: This position may be remote within the United States or hybrid; residence near Saugerties, New York, is not required. description: Position Name – Supply Chain Expert / Subject Matter Expert Type of hiring – Subcon/Fulltime Location – Dearborn, MI (Onsite) Job Description: We are seeking a highly experienced Supply Chain Expert / Subject Matter Expert with deep expertise in sourcing and procurement, vendor management, and end-to-end Source-to-Pay (S2P) processes within the automotive industry. The ideal candidate will assess current sourcing and procurement practices, define future-state processes, collaboration touch points, and translate business requirements into practical operating-model and technology solutions. The role requires strong knowledge of strategic sourcing, category management, supplier lifecycle management, contracting, purchasing, invoicing, supplier performance, and procurement analytics, along with the ability to engage business, procurement, finance, legal, technology, and supplier stakeholders. Responsibilities: Lead process discovery, maturity assessment, and transformation initiatives across the end-to-end S2P lifecycle, from demand intake and sourcing through contracting, purchasing, receipt, invoicing, and payment. Define current-state and future-state processes, operating models, governance, policies, controls, and performance measures for sourcing and procurement. Advise on strategic sourcing, spend analysis, category strategy, market intelligence, RFx, e-auctions, bid evaluation, negotiation, contracting, and savings realization. Design and improve supplier lifecycle processes, including onboarding, qualification, segmentation, risk assessment, compliance, performance management, development, and communications and collaboration. Drive vendor-management frameworks covering service levels, scorecards, quality, delivery, cost, innovation, sustainability, financial health, and corrective-action tracking. Translate business needs into functional requirements, process designs, user stories, acceptance criteria, and implementation priorities for procurement platforms and digital solutions. Partner with procurement, supply chain, finance, accounts payable, legal, operations, IT, and suppliers to resolve process gaps and improve adoption. Identify opportunities for standardization, automation, guided buying, catalog adoption, touchless processing, analytics, and compliance improvement. Define and monitor procurement KPIs such as spend under management, sourcing cycle time, negotiated and realized savings, contract coverage, purchase-order compliance, supplier performance, invoice exceptions, and payment cycle time. Support solution evaluation, implementation, testing, data migration, change management, training, deployment, and post-go-live stabilization. Mandatory Skills: Extensive functional knowledge of sourcing and procurement across direct and indirect spend categories in an automotive or complex manufacturing environment. Strong understanding of the complete S2P / P2P process, including intake, sourcing, contracting, requisitioning, purchase orders, goods or service receipt, invoicing, exception handling, and payment. Hands-on expertise in strategic sourcing, category management, supplier relationship management, vendor risk, contract management, and procurement analytics. Experience defining procurement policies, controls, approval matrices, delegation of authority, compliance mechanisms, and governance forums. Ability to facilitate workshops, map processes, identify pain points, define requirements, and develop pragmatic transformation roadmaps. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret spend, supplier, contract, purchase-order, invoice, and performance data. Excellent communication, consulting, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence senior business and functional leaders. Preferred Skills: Experience with leading procurement platforms such as SAP Ariba, Coupa, Ivalua, Jaggaer, GEP SMART, Oracle Procurement, or equivalent solutions. Understanding of ERP integration, supplier master data, catalogs, contract repositories, tax, accounts payable, and payment processes. Knowledge of automotive procurement practices, supplier quality requirements, regulatory expectations, and global supply-market dynamics. Experience with procurement transformation, shared services, global process ownership, or procurement centre-of-excellence models. Familiarity with data visualization, spend analytics, workflow automation, AI-enabled procurement, and supplier-risk intelligence tools. Experience working with global, cross-functional, and multicultural teams. Qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Finance, Operations, or a related field; a Master’s degree is preferred and added advantage. 10-15 Years of relevant experience in sourcing, procurement, supplier management, or procurement transformation, preferably within automotive or manufacturing. Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional S2P improvement or digital-transformation programmes. Relevant certifications such as CPSM, CIPS, CSCP, PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or procurement-platform certifications are an advantage.

description: If you’re passionate about being part of a dynamic organization that enables a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales to drive innovation and adopt new technologies that deliver business results, then Nationwide’s Technology team could be the place for you! Whether working to enable the processes that support buying decisions or finding the best supplier, price or contract terms, we bring expertise, skill and talent to the task. If you are collaborative, a top-level communicator, highly ethical and have the ability to manage key relationships by providing outstanding service, we want to know more about you! Conducts advanced, continuous industry research and benchmark analysis within a defined spend category. Establishes a category strategy for a highly technical domain, monitors purchasing trends and identifies top suppliers and innovations within the category. Works with Business Partners to manage Business Unit and Procurement relationship by building forecasts of demand, service levels requirements, Total Cost of Ownership models, contractual and other risk requirements (by category domain, actual and forecasted spend), identifying cost reduction opportunities, and developing recommendations. Mentors and trains new associates on Procurement policy, processes and helps them develop Sourcing Skills. May Perform Other Responsibilities As Assigned. description: We are seeking a Principal Category Manager to join our global Procurement team, where innovation knows no borders. This team ensures our enterprise operates with efficiency, high quality, and optimal commercial performance across all third-party supplier partnerships. It connects business strategy with market intelligence and rigorous spend analysis to mitigate risk, optimize supplier value, and drive sustainable growth. With an inclusive culture and flexible work environment, we work together with boldness, curiosity and commitment so we can all win together. As a Principal Category Manager, you will serve as a strategic architect and trusted advisor providing end-to-end category ownership across third-party service suppliers, with a strong focus on Professional Services and Labor. You will oversee supplier selection, complex commercial redlines, contract lifecycle planning, and risk assessment coordination across global business units. You will possess broad decision-making autonomy at the project level to execute strategic sourcing opportunities, optimize workflows, and build cross-functional alignment across Legal, Contracts, Risk, Security, and executive stakeholders. What you'll do Lead the end-to-end procurement lifecycle for third-party services, directing intake, pipeline management, commercial negotiations, pricing structures, and redlining to secure execution. Direct deep spend analyses, market intelligence, and contract portfolio reviews across the Professional Services and Labor categories to capture tangible cost-savings and business efficiencies. Coordinate and lead comprehensive Risk Assessment processes across Legal, Risk, Compliance, and Security partners to resolve potential execution barriers and eliminate enterprise risk prior to contract execution. Act as an expert advisory sounding board for business stakeholders, guiding cross-functional teams on category trends, sourcing pathways, and practical risk mitigation strategies. Partner with Procurement leadership and internal stakeholders to drive enterprise-wide workflow standardization, leveraging automation and procurement systems like SAP and Coupa to eliminate operational friction. What You'll Bring Required Qualifications Minimum 5–7 years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, or supply chain management with demonstrated category expertise in Professional Services. Direct capability in designing and executing complex RFx processes, commercial negotiations, custom Excel financial models, and commercial redlines. Hands-on experience with ERP, Contract Management, and Purchasing systems (such as SAP or Coupa). Proven success managing cross-functional alignment across Legal, Risk, Security, and executive business partners while balancing competing deadlines and priorities. Preferred Qualifications Expertise in the Labor category. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, or a related discipline. Benefits that support you Benefits We know support looks different for everyone. That is why Sabre offers benefits beyond medical and financial coverage, with programs designed to support your well-being, growth and life outside work: Competitive pay and performance-based bonuses Flexible work options Comprehensive healthcare coverage Generous PTO and holidays Strong retirement planning support Family-friendly benefits Professional development opportunities
